title: Machine learning prediction of deep vein thrombosis before staged surgery in lower-leg and ankle fractures treated with temporary external fixation
summary: Naive Bayes predicted DVT before staged lower-limb/ankle surgery in 356 patients; held-out validation AUC was 0.807 (95% CI 0.705–0.909), with low precision-recall AUC 0.343 and optimism-corrected AUC 0.773. This is a small retrospective risk-stratification result, not a validated clinical tool.
ai_technology: Boruta feature selection plus 12 classifiers; Naive Bayes selected on clinical predictors and interpreted with SHAP.
organization: Department of Orthopaedic Surgery, Zhangzhou Affiliated Hospital of Fujian Medical University, China

evidence.tested: Naive Bayes predicted DVT before staged lower-limb/ankle surgery in 356 patients; held-out validation AUC was 0.807 (95% CI 0.705–0.909), with low precision-recall AUC 0.343 and optimism-corrected AUC 0.773. This is a small retrospective risk-stratification result, not a validated clinical tool. Stratified 70/30 split (106 validation patients), five-fold development CV, 500 bootstrap optimism correction, calibration and decision curves.
